description: The catalog's checks grouped into projects, the pieces of work an administrator would plan, and what each project waits on. needs: the other project has to be finished first, or this one causes harm or cannot work. after: recommended order, not a requirement. Every check belongs to exactly one project. The report turns this into a plan for one tenant: the projects with something to fix, in the order they can start.

projects.name: Break-glass accounts
projects.what: Two emergency administrator accounts that every blocking policy leaves out, tested on a schedule.

projects.name: MFA for everyone
projects.what: Every member has a second factor registered and every sign-in asks for one.

needs.why: A sign-in policy that misfires locks everyone out, administrators included; the emergency accounts are the way back in.

projects.name: Block legacy and device-code sign-in
projects.what: Old protocols and the device-code flow, which skip the second factor, are turned off.

needs.why: A sign-in policy that misfires locks everyone out, administrators included; the emergency accounts are the way back in.

projects.name: Phishing-resistant sign-in
projects.what: Passkeys and Authenticator with context replace SMS and voice, and administrators sign in with a method that cannot be phished.

needs.why: People need a second factor registered before the weaker ones are taken away or a stronger one is required.

projects.name: Risk-based access
projects.what: A risky sign-in is challenged and a compromised account is contained.

needs.why: A risky sign-in is answered with a second factor, which people must already have.

projects.name: Least-privilege administration
projects.what: Few standing administrators, separate cloud-only admin accounts, roles activated when needed and reviewed.

needs.why: Removing standing roles and adding activation steps is when administrators get locked out; the emergency accounts are the way back in.

projects.name: Conditional Access upkeep
projects.what: No policy left in report-only or disabled, exclusions kept small, names that say what a policy does.

projects.name: Apps and consent
projects.what: People cannot grant apps access on their own, a workflow takes their requests, and app credentials and owners are kept current.

projects.name: Guests and external access
projects.what: Who can invite guests, what guests can see, and reviews that remove the ones no longer needed.

projects.name: Passwords
projects.what: Passwords that do not expire on a schedule, with banned words refused in the cloud and on-premises.

needs.why: A password that never expires is only safe once every sign-in also asks for a second factor.

projects.name: Joiners, movers and leavers
projects.what: Accounts created from HR, access removed when people leave, inactive accounts found.

projects.name: Audit logs and monitoring
projects.what: Sign-in, audit and activity logs kept and sent somewhere that is watched.

projects.name: Backup and recovery
projects.what: A decision on backup, backups that cannot be deleted quietly, and a way to bring back what was removed.

projects.name: Operations upkeep
projects.what: Expiry dates, Microsoft's announcements and health alerts each have an owner.

projects.name: Bring devices under management
projects.what: Every work device enrolled in Intune, the old management paths retired, stale records cleaned up.

projects.name: Device compliance
projects.what: Every device is judged by a compliance policy, and one without a policy counts as noncompliant.

needs.why: A device has to be enrolled before a compliance policy can judge it.

projects.name: Require compliant devices
projects.what: Company data opens only on a device the organisation manages and judges healthy, with sessions bound to that device.

needs.why: Requiring a compliant device blocks everyone whose device has not been judged yet.
A sign-in policy that misfires locks everyone out, administrators included; the emergency accounts are the way back in.

after.why: Compliance should already know when Defender rates a device at risk before access depends on it.

projects.name: Disk encryption
projects.what: BitLocker and FileVault on every computer, with the recovery keys kept in the directory.

needs.why: A policy reaches a device only once the device is enrolled and managed.

projects.name: Device hardening
projects.what: Security baselines, firewall, SmartScreen, macro blocking, update deadlines and a managed local administrator password.

needs.why: A policy reaches a device only once the device is enrolled and managed.

projects.name: Defender for Endpoint
projects.what: Every device onboarded with antivirus, tamper protection and network protection on, device risk fed into compliance, and open vulnerabilities and incidents worked.

needs.why: A policy reaches a device only once the device is enrolled and managed.

projects.name: Attack surface reduction
projects.what: The rules that stop common malware techniques, set to block, with exclusions written down.

needs.why: The rules run inside Defender Antivirus, which has to be the active antivirus first.

projects.name: Passwordless on computers
projects.what: Windows Hello, cloud Kerberos trust and Platform SSO, so people unlock their computer without typing a password.

needs.why: A policy reaches a device only once the device is enrolled and managed.

after.why: The stronger methods are easier to roll out once people already use them to sign in.

projects.name: Work apps on phones
projects.what: App protection for work apps on phones, with jailbroken and rooted devices blocked.

projects.name: Mail authentication
projects.what: SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MTA-STS, so nobody else can send mail as your domains.

projects.name: Mail filtering
projects.what: The preset policies for everyone, impersonation protection, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and a phishing drill.

after.why: How spoofed mail is treated depends on your own domains authenticating properly first.

projects.name: Mail flow and mailbox access
projects.what: No quiet forwarding, no allow lists that skip filtering, connectors and direct sending closed to strangers.

after.why: Rejecting unauthenticated mail is safe only once your own senders pass authentication.

projects.name: Sharing in SharePoint and OneDrive
projects.what: Sharing limited to named people by default, links that expire, and sync and sessions kept to the organisation's own computers.

projects.name: Teams external access and apps
projects.what: Who outside can reach your people in Teams, who waits in the lobby, and which apps are allowed.

projects.name: Site and group ownership
projects.what: Every site and group has an owner, groups expire when unused, and the most exposed sites are reviewed.

projects.name: Sensitivity labels
projects.what: Labels defined and published to everyone, applied to sites and Teams, and applied automatically where the content is clear.

projects.name: Data loss prevention and retention
projects.what: Policies that stop sensitive content leaving, keep what must be kept, and flag risky handling.

needs.why: The policies act on labels, so the labels have to be published first.

projects.name: Copilot readiness
projects.what: Oversharing found and fixed, restricted search and discovery where needed, and Copilot's own settings governed.

needs.why: Copilot shows people whatever they can already open, so sharing has to be tightened first.
Labels are what keep Copilot from carrying protected content into new documents.

after.why: Access reviews go to site owners, so sites need owners first.
A data loss prevention policy for Copilot builds on the policies already in place.

projects.name: Active Directory: privileged access
projects.what: Few Domain Admins, empty schema and enterprise groups, and admin accounts that cannot be delegated or roasted.

projects.name: Active Directory: Kerberos and credentials
projects.what: Keys rotated, no unconstrained delegation, no roastable accounts, no certificate templates or policies that hand out credentials.

projects.name: Active Directory: platform and sync
projects.what: Supported domain controllers and functional levels, password hash sync, and cloud access managed in Entra.

projects.name: Azure foundations
projects.what: Management groups, policy and tags on every subscription, a security contact, and a budget with an alert.

projects.name: Azure access
projects.what: Few owners, no standing access at the top, and no guest, orphaned or over-broad role assignments.

projects.name: Azure workloads and Defender for Cloud
projects.what: Defender for Cloud on, and key vaults, storage, databases and network ports closed to the internet.

after.why: Plans and policies are assigned through the management groups, which should exist first.

projects.name: Network access
projects.what: Microsoft, internet and private app traffic through Global Secure Access, with the real source address kept for Conditional Access.

projects.name: Easier sign-in for people
projects.what: A sign-in page people recognise, fewer prompts, password reset they can do themselves, and their best method offered first.

projects.name: Smoother devices
projects.what: New computers that set themselves up, OneDrive that signs in by itself, and update restarts with notice.

after.why: These settings arrive through Intune, so devices should be enrolled first.

projects.name: Directory and mail tidy
projects.what: Names, titles and licences kept in order, and Outlook telling people when mail comes from outside.
